about: Which checks of tools/test.sh cover a file: what `tools/test.sh changed` runs for the files
changed. The first rule whose pattern matches a path decides (fnmatch on the path from the
repository's root, where * also matches /). "plugin" is the plugin-check of the plugin whose
folder the path is in; "self" is the changed test module of tests/vpair itself, with every
module that imports it. A path no rule names is reported, and the levels cover it.
The rules are narrow on purpose, and the levels (tools/test.sh all, before every push) cover
what they leave out. A plugin's editor-only files (its EDITOR sources, and the headers that
only they include, or that other sources include only where SPEAKER_HEADLESS is 0) are never
compiled into its headless build, which is what the chain runs: they run the plugin's own
check, not chain. A speakerd file runs `speakerd` and, beside it, only the checks whose
scenarios alone read what the file is for: its log lines, its answers on the command line or
the local link, the PipeWire objects it makes. Where a file only carries what another file is
for (Engine's parameter inbox and its level and timing rings, which Control and Monitor serve;
Main's calls into Control), that other file's rule runs the check. tools/tests/test_impact.py
keeps the map honest: every speakerd file is named by a rule of its own, and every path a
plugin rule without chain names is editor-only.

rules.why: words and drawings
a plugin's editor-only files: in its complete and control builds, never in the headless build the chain runs
one plugin: its SOURCES, DSP, CMakeLists.txt and probes, which its headless build compiles
what every plugin shares

speakerd's audio cycle, which every speakerd scenario plays through; its parameter inbox and its level and timing rings only carry what Control and Monitor serve, whose rules run pair, installers and chain

speakerd's command line and start: --version (the installers refuse one below their minimum and keep its line), the flags the installed unit passes, the device and playing lines smoke reads, the exit on a signal the unit's wrapper records, a shadowed --lv2-bundle refused with status 2; its calls into Control are Control's
speakerd's build and its version, which --version says and the installers check against their minimum
the generated BuildInfo.h: the version and commit --version says, which the installers check and keep as the installed build
device.json: the speakerd scenarios read the limits line; only the installers' scenarios have speakerd read a device.json the installers wrote, and smoke matches that line exactly
the state layers: the speakerd scenarios read `using layer`; only the installers' unit passes --from, and its wrapper's scenario reads `starting at layer ... (--from)`

the PipeWire node: the sink, the links and the quantum the speakerd scenarios play through; the sink speakerd makes without the drop-in (`NO INPUT SINK CONFIGURED`) and the amplifier as the only driver, which the installers' scenarios check; clock.force-quantum, which only pair's buffer_size sets
the local link's socket: ampd's connection (pair, chain's clients alike); its default path and the busy answer, which only smoke's status meets
the local link's operations: ampd's (pair; chain's subscribe and apply are the same ones), and the status with its timing, which only smoke reads
the monitor thread: output/level and the plugins' streams (pair), speakerd/timing (only chain_cost subscribes to it), and the timing lines in the log, which smoke parses
the timing statistics: speakerd/timing's values (chain_cost), the status's timing and the `timing: last <n> s` line (smoke)
a plugin node and its time: every node runs through it (speakerd); its time per node, which only chain_cost asserts
which bundle each plugin runs from, and its build identity in the `plugin node` lines, which only plugin_identity reads
the graph built from a document, which every speakerd scenario plays, and the `plugin node` line it writes for each plugin, which only plugin_identity reads
the graph document: every layer the speakerd scenarios load; its top-level quantum, which only pair's buffer_size gives
the offline render, which the speakerd scenarios compare the live sound with (its `plugin node` lines are GraphBuilder's)
the `speakerd: ` lines: every check reads them, the speakerd scenarios too
speakerd alone: the import of an AudioPluginHost session (speakerd_import, with the examples), the plugins' LV2 state, the sample helpers
a speakerd file no rule above names: everything that runs speakerd, until it is named (tools/tests/test_impact.py fails meanwhile)
